title: v1.2 recruiter additions: a 'How it works' page and an author section on About
audience: recruiters and hiring managers who want, in about a minute, the path from a sensor reading to a maintenance decision, and who built it
rules: The app reads only dashboards/snapshots/; v1.2 adds no snapshot file and changes none, so the snapshot data checksum stays the same.
Every number on the new page comes from a snapshot (facts.json, models.csv, plan.csv, oee_policies.csv) and is recomputed independently from the results files by dashboards/verify_v12.py (CI).
The new page shows its numbers in text, not as metric tiles, so Phase 8's metric comparison (D1.1) needs no new expectations; verify_v12 checks them instead.
Phase 8 stays 5/5, v1.1 stays 5/5 and Phase 9 stays 10/10; their criteria are only extended (the new page joins their page lists), never loosened.
No hand-typed published number on the new page: counts such as sensors kept or features built are not in the snapshots, so the page describes them in words and links the docs.
The author section carries the same facts as the README's Author section (writeup/report_phase9.py) and never an email address or phone number.

how_page.title: How does a sensor reading become a maintenance decision?
how_page.business_question: How does the pipeline turn raw engine sensor data into a crew schedule and a simulated OEE result?

diagram.kind: st.graphviz_chart from a DOT string (rendered in the browser; no new dependency)
diagram.layout: top to bottom, so it stays readable at phone width
diagram.edges: each stage to the next; plus a dashed edge Monitoring -> Forecast labelled 'retrain flag'
diagram.simulated_stage: the OEE stage has a dashed border and '(simulated)' in its label: line style plus text, not colour alone
diagram.text_alternative: the stage sections below the diagram repeat every stage in words

stage_sections.form: one block per stage, in diagram order, each with: What happens, Why it matters, Result, See it (the app page that shows it, by its menu name)

numbers.label: remaining-life cap (cycles)
numbers.independent: clip value in models/predictions_phase5b.csv (as Phase 8 D1.3)

numbers.label: RMSE of the published model and of XGBoost on the FD003 test engines (cycles)
interval level (percent) and number of MC dropout passes
alert threshold (cycles) and engines flagged in FD001 and FD003
numbers.source: facts.json alert_threshold; plan.csv rows per dataset

numbers.label: crews per day, horizon days, engines booked and engines left without a crew, per dataset; solver status
numbers.source: facts.json crews_per_day, horizon_days, solver_status_FD00x; plan.csv scheduled_day, status

numbers.label: pooled simulated OEE (percent, 1 decimal) and unplanned failures for predictive, fixed interval and run to failure

how_page.honesty: the Monitoring stage says plainly that the drift rule failed its false-alarm target on FD004 and that the Phase 7 target was not met; the OEE stage and the diagram say 'simulated'

author_section.where: About and method page, a section headed 'About the author', placed first on the page, above the data checksum
